chunk_map.heading: Save the rule if it earned itself

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 5 "Save the rule if it earned itself": line 42: "If a branch from the second-pass read sharpened how plans get made..." — "second-pass read" is never named in this file's own prior chunks (0-4), but per rule 1's module-include-order carve-out the composed deck inserts the linked exercise `push-back-on-the-plan.md` (chunk 4's 'Exercise: Push back on the plan' link) directly before this section, and that exercise repeatedly names "second-pass read"/"second-pass grilling" (verified via grep, lines 5, 62, 68, 111, 117, 123, 235 of that file). Harm (reader can't resolve the term) is not present in the actual sequential room read. Also checked chunk 5 line 42 "that one branch" — "branch" is named in chunk 3 (What You'll Learn, line 20: "Walk down unresolved branches"), a clean same-file resolution, not a violation. "these rules" at chunk 5 line 38 resolves against "the task-shaping rule" named in chunk 4's exercise link title (line 34). No chunk left a referent genuinely unresolved.

grep for 'this page'/'above'/'below'/positional phrasing over the body returned nothing (see rule 12 mechanical check). All cross-file references name the source directly: chunk 2 line 14 names Cherny's video, Horthy's essay ("this is the module it pays off in"), and the reference page by its own link text; chunk 4 names each lecture/exercise by title in its own link. No file is located by deck position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n "you did|you saw|you caught|you named|you ran|the run you|the session you" (lines 1-92)` → no matches. This file's body contains no "the X you did/saw" backward-beat phrasing to check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n "guess|predict|reveal" (lines 1-92)` → no matches. No guess-before-reveal beat exists in this module file to check ordering against.

Closest candidate: chunk 8/9 ("Pre-reads before Module 3/4") — short at 2 short paragraphs each, but each carries a self-carrying claim (what to read and why it matters for the next module), not a bare wait-state. Every other chunk (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10) carries either a stated claim (Big Idea), an instruction (Prework, Start here), an LO list, or a closing move (Save the rule, Next). None is a lone context-dependent bullet.

Every `##` in this file is a fixed architecture-mandated module-section name (Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn, Start here, Save the rule if it earned itself, Key Concepts, Optional challenges, Pre-reads before Module N, Next) per `check_student_facing.md §17`, not a claim-style header rule 6 tests for literal truth. None of these headers assert a proposition the chunk could contradict.

Closest candidate: chunk 6 (Key Concepts) line 57: "Assume about 10% of it is wrong and go find which part." — a bare number with no attached retraction clause in THIS body (the paired "could be more or less" hedge lives only in `orient-and-introspect.md`, delegated per the maintainer block line 105), so the number+retraction sub-item doesn't even trigger (it requires both a number AND its own retraction in the same beat). No "Not X. Not Y. Z." constructions, anaphora/epistrophe triples, self-grading superlatives, abstraction-noun stacks, or empty-leg verb triplets found anywhere in the body (checked all 11 chunks by read).

rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 2 line 10 "Surface one multi-file backlog task" — "Surface" is the ordinary engineering verb ("surface the issue"), explicitly exempted by rule 8's own carve-out, not the repo-internal noun sense. No instance of compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, or Connections-as-proper-noun anywhere in the body (grep clean).

Not an epic.**") and chunk 10 line 89 ("**Pick one scoped task...**") are whole-sentence bolded task-sizing callouts, matching the `check_pedagogy.md §34` exception verbatim, and are accept-noted in the maintainer block (line 99: "mandated, not stylistic"). Chunk 3's five `- **[verb]** [thing]` bullets are the mandated `module-shape.md` LO template, each bold span one word, N/A per rule 9's own template carve-out. No other chunk carries more than 0-1 bolded spans.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/slides.test.js` → 24/24 pass including anchor-resolution and click-navigation tests, and `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/plan-mode-done-right.md` → "files: 1 slides: 9 oversized: 0", confirming the renderer counts and measures 9 slides from this exact file. This is a module file, which is a top-level `section.module` in `site/layouts/slides.js:245` (`root.querySelectorAll(':scope > section.module')`), so the whole body reaches the composed deck by construction — no phase-less section to strand.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule 13 states there is currently "no rule" on link value (the open question was resolved to a non-issue on 2026-08-12) — only the settled naming convention binds ("name the document in the link text"), which every link in chunk 4 and chunk 2 satisfies (e.g. "[Lecture: The whole map]", "[Exercise: Push back on the plan]"). Explicitly a review surface, never a gate, so no REVISE is available under this rule.
